title: Shared fact check: literal, independent judge, source strength; research packets first
description:
MODULE `src/papyrus_content/fact_check.py`, contract `fact-check/v1`, usable by any generator. `check_claims(claims, sources, *, judge=None) -> {contract, counts, claims:[{claim, sources, verdict, literal:{unmatched:[...]}, judge:{verdict, quote, explanation, quoteVerified}, reasons:[...]}]}`. `sources` maps a source id to its text (for research: title plus snippets, because the writer is told to use only those). Pure and no I/O except the injected judge.

LITERAL CHECK. Extract from each claim: proper-name runs, numbers with units (%, $, counts), years and dates, and quoted strings. Each must appear in the union of the texts of the sources that claim cites. Normalize case, diacritics, curly quotes, hyphens, commas in numbers ("$200,000" = "200,000"). All tokens of a name must be found: "Rodney Reid" with only "Reid" in the source fails on "Rodney". "Tennessee" absent from the source fails. Skip ordinary capitalized words: sentence-initial words not otherwise found as names, months, and a small list of generic words found by reading real claims, not guessed. Measure false flags on the three real packets (below) and tune, reporting what you changed.

JUDGE. `llm_judge(llm)`: one call per claim, thread pool limited only by provider rate limits, model `DEFAULT_LLM_MODEL`. System prompt tells it nothing about how the claim was written. Input: claim and cited source texts only. JSON schema: verdict `supported | partly_supported | not_supported | source_silent`, `quote` (verbatim from the source), `explanation`. Code verifies the quote appears (normalized) in the cited text; a quote that doesn't appear makes the verdict `not_supported` with reason `quote_not_in_source`. Also asks: does the claim state as fact something the source only attributes to a party (allegation, press release)? `attribution_lost` boolean.

OVERALL VERDICT per claim. `verified` needs a literal pass AND judge `supported` with a verified quote AND not attribution_lost. Otherwise `unverified` with reasons. Judge unavailable or failed: `unchecked`, never verified. Literal failure cannot be overridden by the judge.

SOURCE STRENGTH. Per claim: count of distinct registered domains cited, `singleSource` boolean. Nothing fails on this; it is reported. Packet-level: which sources carry the most claims.

RESEARCH WIRING (`multi_search_research.py`, runs with a Story; no-Story runs too, since the check applies to any packet). After synthesis:
- `claims` keeps verified claims only. `unverifiedClaims` holds the rest with reasons. Disagreement positions get the literal check; a failing position is labelled, not removed.
- Summary and recommended angle are rewritten by one model call from verified claims only, so a failed claim cannot survive in the summary. The rewrite also goes through the literal check against all verified claims' sources; if it fails, use a plain code-built summary listing verified claim counts rather than the failing text.
- Packet gets `factCheck` (counts and per-claim results). The packet body shows verified claims, then a labelled "Could not verify" section with reasons.
- Cited-only intake counts verified claims and disagreement positions only.
- `prior_research` layer in `newsroom_context_pack.py` shows verified claims as claims and unverified ones labelled "Unverified, do not rely on".
- Failed judge calls do not fail the run; they make `unchecked`. Record counts in the completed event.

REPLAY. `papyrus assignments fact-check --message <research packet message id> [--judge true|false] [--format text|json]`: read-only, reads the packet through `load_assignment_research_packet_entries` or the attachment, runs the check, writes nothing. Its purpose is measuring old packets.

SPECS. Gherkin `features_backend/fact-check.feature`, narrative, with synthetic content and fake judge: an invented first name fails the literal check; an invented place fails; number formats match; a judge quote not in the source demotes; judge failure gives unchecked; literal failure overrides a supportive judge; an allegation stated as fact is flagged; failed claims leave `claims` and appear labelled; summary contains no failed claim; intake skips sources cited only by failed claims; later pack labels them. Add `docs/fact-checking.md` describing all layers honestly, what is built and what isn't. No network and no real content in tests. No production writes.

REAL-DATA MEASURE. Three real packets are saved locally for the literal check, offline and free. Metadata files, field `research`: /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-home-Projects/01ea45fd-85a1-432a-89a4-a99b8de4198e/scratchpad/packet/metadata.json, .../packet2/metadata.json, .../packet3/metadata.json. Source index to URL is in `multiSearch.sourceProviders`; snippets by URL are in `proposedReferences`. Report per packet: claims flagged, and each flagged term with the claim. Packet 3 must flag "Rodney" and "Tennessee" on those two claims. Read each flag and say whether it is a true catch or a false flag. These contain real content: do not copy them into the repo or tests.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Live on packet 3, three judge passes: 12 verified, 8-9 needs_check, 7-8 rejected. Lipps attribution and Parks nuance caught again; Rodney and Tennessee rejected in every run. Remaining instability seen: one claim moved between needs_check and rejected, none crossed into verified in these two runs. Research packets are wired; fact check runs on the next research run.
